thread:
maya: Quick sync — planning to enable feature flag routing_experiment_v2 as a canary to run an A/B test between routing strategy A (baseline) and B (new heuristic). Proposal: 5% global canary, within that 50/50 A/B, run for 2h. Looking for guardrail suggestions: metrics, stopping rules, rollout steps, and who owns rollback. cc @sam @li @oliver

sam: +1 on canary. Metrics to monitor: p50 latency, p95 latency, error_rate (4xx/5xx), request_drop, alignment_score (quality), cost_per_token. Also track fallback_rate and user_facing_errors.

li: Agree with sam. Add: track request path distribution and cache hit rate. Stopping rule ideas: if p95 latency increases >20% absolute OR error_rate increases >0.5% absolute OR alignment_score drops >3 points. Also auto-kill on 5xx spike (>0.2% absolute over baseline for 5m).

oliver: For audience split: do 5% of global users, then within that random 50/50 to avoid confounders. Ensure we tag logs: experiment=routing_v2_canary. Who will create the experiment in the framework? @eng-platform-bot

eng-platform-bot: reminder — experiment ids must be unique. Suggested id: routing_v2_canary_20240731. I will create a dashboard template, hook telemetry, and add an alert if error_rate delta >0.3% over baseline for 10m. Auto-kill can be enabled per config.

maya: Thanks. Draft config I'm planning to deploy:

```json
{
  "flag": "routing_experiment_v2",
  "audience": "global",
  "canary_pct": 5,
  "variants": {
    "A": 0.5,
    "B": 0.5
  },
  "duration_minutes": 120,
  "kill_conditions": {
    "p95_latency_increase_pct": 20,
    "error_rate_absolute_increase": 0.5
  },
  "owner": "maya",
  "oncall_for_rollback": "sre-oncall"
}
```

sam: add metric hooks before deploy: telemetry.event('experiment.assign', {experiment_id, user_id, variant}). Ensure logs include experiment_id in request tracing. Also require manual approval to go above 5% to 20%.

oliver: Can we set automatic rollback for the strict kill conditions but require human approval for any expansion beyond initial canary? I think auto-kill + human approval for scaling is safe.

eng-platform-bot: noted. Auto-kill: enabled. Auto-scale blocked — requires workflow approval. Also configuring fallback: if B's latency > baseline by 15% for 3 consecutive minutes, route those requests to baseline variant automatically.

deploy-bot: deploy plan: staging rollout at 2024-07-31T15:10Z (smoke + integ checks), prod canary at 2024-07-31T15:30Z to 5%. If staging checks pass, will flip staging -> prod timeline.

maya: I'll run the quality eval set after 1 hour into the canary and post results to this thread. Tagging @li for SLO review and @sre-oncall for rollback readiness.

sre-oncall: I'll standby during the canary window. Ping me immediately if alerts fire. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — executing tomorrow morning. Will post a short postmortem if anything notable happens.
